slides.headline:
Every dish here
is built on a fern.
slides.subline: Gosari Express, Sindang — a vegan noodle shop inside a traditional market, newly awarded both a Bib Gourmand and a MICHELIN Green Star

slides.label: MICHELIN Green Stars in all of Korea — Gosari Express is one of them
slides.note: In the MICHELIN Guide Seoul & Busan 2026, Gosari Express and Mitou were newly awarded the Green Star for sustainable gastronomy, joining Gigas in Seoul and Fiotto in Busan. The same guide named Gosari Express a new Bib Gourmand — one of eight added to a 71-restaurant list. Source: guide.michelin.com

items.d: Gosari is the young shoot of the bracken fern, foraged in spring, then blanched and dried. Rehydrated, it turns dark and gently chewy

items.t: Usually a side, never the point
items.d: It sits in almost every bibimbap and on ancestral-rite tables, as one small brown heap among many. Most Korean diners have eaten it hundreds of times without ordering it once

items.t: Here it carries the whole menu
items.d: The kitchen developed a gosari oil sauce and put it at the centre of an entirely plant-based list — from spicy bibim noodles to Taiwanese-style pancakes, per the MICHELIN Guide's own description

items.t: The stated motto is ordinary, on purpose
items.d: "Vegetarianism in everyday life." Not a wellness pitch, not a tasting menu — a noodle shop meant to be eaten at with a drink

slides.title:
It moved to the harder
neighbourhood on purpose.
slides.body:
The first version was a pop-up called Gosari by Bad Carrot in Mangwon-dong, serving a single pasta in a room of about ten seats, with the day's vegetables chosen from whatever was in season. It worked. Mangwon is also a district where vegetarian food already had an audience.

So the founder, Kim Je-eun, left it. Gosari Express opened in June 2024 inside Seoul Jungang Market in Sindang-dong — a traditional market with no vegetarian restaurants and a customer base of every age. The pasta became noodles, because noodles are what a market eats. Korean coverage reports that some of the original following did not follow, and that neighbourhood regulars turned up instead, some of them keeping their own bottles of makgeolli at the shop.

That is the part worth noticing. Plant-based cooking in Korea usually asks to be treated as a category. This one asked to be treated as lunch, in a market, next to everyone else — and then collected a Bib Gourmand and a Green Star in the same guide.

items.d: Ground floor, inside Seoul Jungang Market — roughly two minutes from Sindang Station Exit 2. Phone 0507-1393-3140
Closed Sunday and Monday, with a mid-afternoon break and last order around 20:30, per its DiningCode listing. Confirm before travelling
Listed prices include the Gosari Classic at 11,000 won, perilla-seed gosari bibim noodles at 18,000, grilled baby cabbage at 13,000 and gosari noodle tteokbokki at 25,000

items.t: It is built for a drink with the meal
items.d: Korean write-ups describe it as a vegetarian noodle shop designed around banju — a glass alongside the food rather than after it. Oat-milk ice cream, 9,000 won, closes it

slides.text:
This is research, not a personal review.
Every fact here comes from published sources, checked in September 2026.
slides.by:
We have not eaten here. Whether fern-based cooking is to your taste is entirely your call, not ours.
A small market shop with a new MICHELIN listing can mean queues. Prices, hours and menus change without notice — confirm before you go.

caption:
A vegan noodle shop inside a Seoul traditional market just took two MICHELIN nods at once.

Gosari Express, in Sindang's Seoul Jungang Market, builds an entirely plant-based menu on bracken fern. The 2026 guide gave it a Bib Gourmand and one of Korea's four Green Stars.

We haven't eaten here, and taste is yours to judge.

Sources in the last slide.
